items.headline: Meta debuts "Muse Wonder" AI model in fresh test of users' willingness to pay
items.summary: Meta introduced a new AI model, Muse Wonder, as part of a continued push to get users to pay for its AI agent products built on the Muse personal-agent platform it launched in September. The move underscores how major labs are increasingly testing subscription and paywall models for advanced agent features.

items.headline: OpenAI brings GPT-6 and a new "Intelligent UI" to all ChatGPT users
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out its GPT-6 models -- Sol for paid tiers, Luna for free users -- to ChatGPT's more than 1.2 billion weekly users, alongside an "Intelligent UI" that lets responses include charts, buttons and other interactive elements instead of plain text. The update covers standard Chat but leaves OpenAI's separate Work and Codex models unchanged.

items.headline: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT for Teens an "Unacceptable Risk"
items.summary: After running more than 4,000 test prompts on teen accounts, the child-safety nonprofit found ChatGPT for Teens failed to reliably flag self-harm and suicidal-ideation signals and saw crisis-hotline referrals drop after OpenAI's August teen-safety update; it is urging OpenAI to restrict the product to adults until the gaps are fixed. OpenAI disputes the testing methodology.

items.headline: White House unveils $2.4 billion in AI compute pledges for its Genesis Mission
items.summary: Eleven companies led by Nvidia ($1B) and AMD ($500M), along with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, pledged a combined $2.4 billion in computing credits and AI tools to federal science agencies under the administration's Genesis Mission initiative, part of a broader $6 billion science package meant to support more than 15 federal agencies.

items.headline: AI startups raised $1.81 billion across 46 funding rounds in a single day
items.summary: A daily funding tracker counted 46 AI-related venture rounds closing on October 8, led by Chinese model lab Butterfly Effect's $500 million Series C and US agent startup Arena's $200 million Series B, underscoring how capital keeps flooding into AI despite growing questions about an investment bubble.

items.headline: Lawsuit accuses OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI of an illegal "AI slowdown pact"
items.summary: A proposed class action filed in the Northern District of California alleges the four companies violated US antitrust law by coordinating to slow AI development following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's September safety essay, arguing the alleged pact reduces the value consumers get from paid AI subscriptions to Claude, ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini.

items.headline: SemiAnalysis: China's AI data center capacity is closing in on the US
items.summary: A SemiAnalysis report estimates mainland China's delivered AI data center capacity at over 24 gigawatts against roughly 56 gigawatts in the US, with another 50GW in China either under construction or announced, suggesting the compute gap between the two countries is narrowing faster than widely assumed.

items.headline: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over AI training
items.summary: The two news organizations filed suit in federal court in Manhattan alleging OpenAI and Microsoft scraped their paywalled articles to train and run ChatGPT, Copilot and Bing AI features, seeking destruction of the implicated training data and models plus damages, in a case that echoes The New York Times' earlier suit against the companies.
